newsitem.title: USA: Mutual Savings wants assessment exemption.
newsitem.headline: Mutual Savings wants assessment exemption.

text.p: Mutual Savings Bank said it applied to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation for an exemption from a special assessment by the Deposit Insurance Funds Act of 1996.

If the request were not granted, Mutual Savings said it would pay a special assessment of $3 million on November 27, 1996, or $0.71 a share. The assessment would be accrued as an expense as of September 30, 1996.
The company said it would not record the assessment net of income taxes because of its current net operating loss carryforward.
Mutual Savings said it estimates the benefit of being exempted from the special assessment and instead paying the regular semi-annual assessments as about $1.9 million.

The company said it believes it qualifies for exemptions under Section 2702 (f)(1) of the Funds Act. Chief Executive Officer Robert Shuster declined to provide more details, saying regulatory restrictions bar the company from disclosing certain risk classifications.
